anchors.quote: ownership is um a very very important part like what did you personally own in the project project what did you personally do for the product
your impact you know what what changed because of you
it all boils down to what problems have you solved for the company
what impact have you had in the business since they've hired you what did you personally own versus the wider team

claim_en: For startup clients the recruiter judges a candidate by what problems they solved, the impact they had and what they personally owned versus the wider team.

anchors.quote: you also need to have some sort of breadth across the stack you can't just be too focused on databases

claim_en: Startup candidates need some breadth across the stack rather than a narrow focus on databases, React or backend alone.

anchors.quote: imagine the interviewer is probably thinking can I put this engineer in front of stakeholders can this engineer communicate

claim_en: In interviews, assume the interviewer is asking whether the engineer can be put in front of stakeholders, communicate and build relationships.

anchors.quote: a few things that I look for instantly is where you've worked for

claim_en: On the first look the recruiter checks where the candidate has worked.

anchors.quote: your education your recent roles your tech stack

claim_en: Education is among the things the recruiter looks at first.
notes: The same list names recent roles (SCR-2) and the tech stack (NEW-2).

anchors.quote: your education your recent roles

claim_en: Recent roles are among the things the recruiter looks at first.

anchors.quote: your recent roles your tech stack

claim_en: The tech stack is among the things the recruiter looks at first.

anchors.quote: what stage your company's at whether it's a preede a seed series ABC BC what what sort of funding rounds have they gone through how long have you stayed through those funding rounds
any of the companies VC backing how much they've raised also strong signals for for other UK startups to hire you

claim_en: The recruiter checks each company's stage and funding rounds and how long the candidate stayed through them; VC backing and money raised are strong signals for other UK startups.

anchors.quote: what has your progression been like um so if you were there for two years and you were promoted to a senior that's usually a good signal for me

claim_en: Progression is checked: a promotion to senior within two years is usually a good signal.

anchors.quote: very like old school wordy CVs where it's like four or five pages long

claim_en: For the recruiter's market, old-school wordy CVs of four or five pages are a red flag.

anchors.quote: when you don't explain the gaps and short stints in in your CV

claim_en: Unexplained gaps and short stints on the CV are a red flag.

anchors.quote: if you list a bunch of technologies but there's no context as to like where you've used these technologies sort of what specific languages or specific frameworks have you used at each company

claim_en: Listing a bunch of technologies without saying where they were used, which languages and frameworks at each company, is a red flag.

anchors.quote: anything like typos or or or anything like that you know kind of immediately uh puts a red flag

claim_en: Typos immediately put a red flag in the recruiter's mind.

anchors.quote: you are like senior level I would say two pages max two pages is the general sweet spot I I say everybody should aim for
I would say try and aim for two as a general rule of thumb

claim_en: Two pages is the general sweet spot everybody should aim for; at senior level two pages is the maximum.

anchors.quote: if you are a junior uh and you don't have a lot of experience one page should be enough

claim_en: For a junior without much experience one page should be enough.

anchors.quote: if you are a very very experienced engineer like a CTO or a VP then you know maybe having it slightly longer isn't a problem

claim_en: For a very experienced engineer such as a CTO or VP, a CV slightly longer than two pages is not a problem.

value.condition: very experienced engineer, CTO or VP

anchors.quote: you don't need to go into detail of all your roles especially if your first few roles aren't relevant to the job that you're applying for

claim_en: Do not go into detail on every role, especially early roles not relevant to the job.

anchors.quote: you should always lead with the outcomes in plain English and then follow with the technical details
a non-technical person like myself can read it and realize the good work you've done and then the technical person can sort of dive into the specific technologies

claim_en: Lead with the outcomes in plain English and follow with the technical details, so a non-technical recruiter and a technical reader both understand.

anchors.quote: saw problem X created solution Y which led to you know I don't know like a reducing load times by 40%
a product mindset uh high ownership you know um knowing the impact and labeling that very clearly on your CV

claim_en: Write achievements as problem, solution and result, for example a problem solved by server side rendering that cut load times by 40% and achieved a business outcome; label the impact very clearly on the CV.

anchors.quote: if you've worked with any startups as well sort of building a product from 0ero to one sometimes having literally zero to one in your CV helps a lot

claim_en: For startups, having built a product from zero to one, and saying literally zero to one on the CV, helps a lot.

anchors.quote: anything that's like a genuine interest as well that's like a side project or like a hackathon that you've been to showing passion for your work is is always a good idea

claim_en: Showing genuine interest through a side project or a hackathon is always a good idea.

anchors.quote: a typical like general interview process we're seeing in the market is usually four to five stages
this can usually last you know anywhere between two to six weeks

claim_en: A typical startup process has four to five stages (recruiter screen, hiring manager technical discussion, technical tests, systems or product design, a chat with the CEO or founder) and lasts two to six weeks.

anchors.quote: it is to not just speak about your tech speak about the problem you identified the problem you solved the commercial impact

claim_en: In interviews, talk about the problem identified and solved and the commercial impact, not just the tech.

anchors.quote: don't start coding before you clarify the problem
even if you get stuck I always tell people think out loud
not clarify the problem not not like coding before clarifying is is bad

claim_en: In technical stages, clarify the problem before writing any code and think out loud.

anchors.quote: I would suggest like not saying we especially if you specifically own the part of the problem um say I

claim_en: Say I rather than we for the parts the candidate personally owned.

anchors.quote: if you're speaking to the hiring manager have a list
people want to figure out how are you leveraging AI nowadays so have a have an answer prepared for that
I'd have a list of your best accomplishments prepared
don't just do research into the company do research into the person that's interviewing you

claim_en: Prepare for the first call: an answer on how AI is used, the hardest technical challenges solved, a list of best accomplishments, and research on the company, its product and the interviewer.

anchors.quote: keep doing things on the side as well uh you know if you're going through interviews and you don't have a job right now keep yourself busy

claim_en: When out of work during a job search, keep doing things on the side; they become material for the next interview.
notes: Said about interviews, not the CV; supports the activity part of GAP-1.

anchors.quote: I think definitely include your LinkedIn and your GitHub

claim_en: Definitely include LinkedIn on the CV, and GitHub when it is active.

anchors.quote: especially you know if your GitHub has a lot of commits and you're very active on it definitely definitely include it
if you literally have no contributions it might end up hurting you
they let's say they have two candidates one has a lot of GitHub contributions one doesn't um you know they might go with the one that does have the contributions
if you're very unactive I would say just include your LinkedIn it should be fine

claim_en: Include GitHub when it has a lot of commits; with no contributions it can end up hurting, since a hiring manager choosing between two candidates might pick the one with contributions, so a very inactive candidate should include only LinkedIn.

anchors.quote: LinkedIn I would say is essential like everyone should have a LinkedIn nowadays
it is you know where I find people it is where I look at your experience uh and you know without a LinkedIn it can be harder

claim_en: LinkedIn is essential: it is where the recruiter finds people and checks their experience, and without it screening is harder.

anchors.quote: I would keep your LinkedIn current i would put like some information as well in your under your LinkedIn of like what you've specifically done for each company

claim_en: Keep LinkedIn current and add what was specifically done at each company.
